mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 1.25% over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 1.25% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses wage growth and consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of at least 0.5% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < -0.5% and HOUST < -0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and HOUST decline by at least 0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 1.0% during a recession signals an aggressive easing cycle, which boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 1.0% and UNRATE > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise of at least 1% in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) in the same month signals a demand expansion, which boosts corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 1% and RSAFS > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS rise by more than 1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE but rising PAYEMS) above 63% for three consecutive months indicates a tighter labor market, which supports wage growth and consumer spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.3% monthly for 3 months AND UNRATE stable (<0.1pp change)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive under the specified labor market tightening conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.4% in industrial production (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion, which raises earnings expectations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO rises by at least 0.4% for four consecutive months.
